correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives \(\frac{d}{dt}[\(m y^2+(z-c)^2\)]=-2b(z-c)\) exactly. Integration, stationarity of compactly supported invariant measures, and Liouville's formula give the finite-time mean, exact invariant mean, determinant identity and asymptotic volume rate. The Lyapunov-sum conclusion uses the standard Oseledets determinant identity. All boundary assumptions are stated; finite numerical spectra are only consistency checks.

final_claim: For the four-dimensional flow \(\dot x=-ay-xz-u\), \(\dot y=x(z-c)\), \(\dot z=-b-mxy\), \(\dot u=kx-y\), with \(b\ne0\), define \(R=m y^2+(z-c)^2\). Along every classical solution, \(\dot R=-2b(z-c)\). Consequently, on every bounded forward solution, \(\lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}\int_0^T z(t)\,dt=c\); every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies \(\int z\,d\mu=c\). Since the divergence is \(-z\), Liouville's formula gives \(\log|\det D\phi_T|=-cT+[R(T)-R(0)]/(2b)\), hence every bounded forward orbit has asymptotic phase-volume rate \(-c\), and every compactly supported ergodic invariant measure has Lyapunov-sum \(\sum_{j=1}^4\lambda_j=-c\) whenever its Lyapunov spectrum is defined. In particular, every periodic orbit has exact period mean \(c\). This upgrades the source's empirical statement that \(c\) is almost positively correlated with the offset of \(z\) to an exact stationary law and explains the reported Lyapunov sums near \(-1\) at \(c=1\) and \(-1.3\) at \(c=1.3\).
